title: HIV, malnutrition, and noncommunicable disease epidemics among tuberculosis-affected households in east and southern Africa: A cross-sectional analysis of the ERASE-TB cohort

en.research_question: The investigation examines the frequency and clustering of HIV infection, nutritional deficits, and chronic noncommunicable conditions among relatives of individuals diagnosed with tuberculosis across three nations in eastern and southern Africa.
en.study_design: Authors performed a cross-sectional evaluation drawing from a larger multicountry cohort to quantify disease occurrence and concurrent diagnoses within targeted family groups.
en.population_setting: The analytical sample comprised 1,958 participants aged ten years or older, representing 786 distinct households located in Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe.
en.main_findings: Substantial portions of the cohort exhibited HIV infection, anemia, elevated blood pressure, and metabolic irregularities, with more than half of adults carrying at least one chronic illness and a quarter experiencing multiple simultaneous diagnoses. Antiretroviral therapy coverage was relatively established for those with HIV, whereas the majority of individuals with noncommunicable diseases remained unidentified and lacked medical management.
en.public_health_relevance: These observations underscore the extensive comorbidity burden residing within tuberculosis-impacted families and indicate that standardized screening protocols could function as practical access points for detecting and addressing overlapping medical needs.
en.limitations: Diagnostic criteria depended on rapid hemoglobin A1c assays for diabetes classification and utilized isolated daily blood pressure readings to establish hypertension status instead of serial assessments.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication supplies foundational epidemiological metrics regarding disease co-occurrence within a defined geographic and familial demographic. It establishes a contextual reference for analyzing how infectious and chronic pathologies may intersect in resource-constrained environments, aiding future literature mapping and gap identification.

zh.research_question: 探讨东非与南部非洲地区结核病受影响家庭中人类免疫缺陷病毒、营养异常及非传染性疾病的流行状况及其共存模式。
zh.study_design: 该工作依托多国联合队列项目开展横断面数据分析，在莫桑比克、坦桑尼亚及津巴布韦对年满十岁的结核病患者密切接触者实施同步筛查。
zh.population_setting: 样本涵盖七百八十六个家庭的一千九百五十八名成员，参与者以女性为主，中位年龄二十七岁，其中极少数同时确诊活动性结核。
zh.main_findings: 数据显示该群体中人类免疫缺陷病毒感染比例为百分之十五，高血压与糖尿病检出率分别达到百分之三十二和百分之九，贫血与体重不足各占百分之十八，超重或肥胖占比百分之二十九。成年人超六成携带至少一项慢性疾病，四分之一呈现多重共病特征，且多数非传染性疾病患者尚未获得规范诊疗。
zh.public_health_relevance: 结果提示结核相关家庭承受着复合型健康压力，把常规慢病评估嵌入结核病排查流程，有望提升高危个体的早期识别率并优化预防性干预路径。
zh.limitations: 研究在疾病界定方法上存在不足，具体表现为依赖床旁血糖化血红蛋白指标判定糖尿病，且高血压诊断仅基于单次门诊测量结果。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献系统梳理了特定地理范围内结核关联家庭的慢性共病基线分布，可作为公共卫生文献检索与背景知识构建的参考资料，用于理解该人群的健康负担结构，但不涉及实时疫情追踪或信号验证。
